Yochanan that shelamim is owner's property and forbids his own as Gemara Tosafot; thereby understand Chullin s.v. ki hein de'amrin in Zevachim on difficulty ne'evad forbade—for person does not forbid, etc.—for R. Huna those are his chatot, etc.; difficulty in conclusion all hold he forbids only “to pain”—must say also per them like R. Huna and Zevachim sugya comes to conclusion—and tzarich iyun apparently. But per what I wrote it works—even in conclusion they lack R. Huna's words d'oraisa person does not forbid—still difficulty why teach animal chatat—and must say chatat as his own; think. I trusted these words have place in halachah—God will enlighten darkness; nevertheless we emerged d'oraisa person does not forbid at all, only d'rabbanan; much difference between Torah and rabbinic issur and between R. Chananel and Rashi; for Torah Rosh decided well.
Also here Choshen Mishpat siman 385—Mechaber rules anonymously like Rambam regarding libating wine and partnership—he forbids and we do not say “to pain him”; all Acharonim wondered why he ruled there like Rambam without mentioning Ra'osh's view; Semag there on wine with partners—he intended to pain friend—he should have given friend's share in separate vessel and mixed and saved his own, unlike animal impossible to divide without slaughter; therefore distinguish; Shach challenged from Gemara words and I defended with good reason.
And not to forbid: Taz seif 4 brought Ran's words that nevertheless his shechitah is not shechitah and he forbids because of nevelah; Maharshal agreed; Taz settled Bach's difficulty from two holding knife—fine wrote—and this deals with stam even if he did not slaughter he only disqualifies any act; if so since he does not make nevelah he does not disqualify; Nekudot HaKesef did not challenge except difficulty Shach hints Mishmeret HaBayit—Taz did not answer at all, and so Nekudot HaKesef. I say to settle difficulty—and Ran and Ra'ah have proof for their ruling: Rashba's difficulty R. Nachman challenged R. Huna who said in any act he forbids—how liable for slaughter outside—here forbidden because of idol worship; R. Nachman should challenge himself person does not forbid; nevertheless since he slaughtered and did act—it is nevelah—how afterward liable for slaughter outside; and what Gemara challenged R. Nachman who holds in act does not forbid—why establish in bird chatat—establish in animal chatat. What difficulty—for in animal chatat once he slaughtered one siman it became nevelah since his shechitah not considered—how liable for slaughter outside—great difficulty. Appears can also settle Gemara there R. Huna challenged from baraita bringing three chatot—one slaughtering for idol worship forbids and no slaughter outside; Gemara answers saying at completion of slaughter he worshiped; Gemara challenges if so should teach “offering”; Rashi explains for first version of difficulty—even R. Nachman who holds person does not forbid even in act—why teach chatat and not offering. Difficulty: was first language of Gemara forgotten in Zevachim—that R. Yishmael b. R. Yochanan shelamim is owner's money—as Rambam; appears difficulty here per Tosafot s.v. ha on mountain that although mountain not made idol worship to forbid offering—nevertheless worker liable death—see there; if so why challenge from baraita—perhaps deals slaughtering for mountain idol worship and b'mezid liable death and b'shogeg brings chatat—nevertheless no offering issur forbidding animal because of idol-worship offering—and plainly liable for slaughter outside—tzarich iyun apparently; to settle must say Tosafot s.v. chayav gimel chatat wrote that which it does not count ten—it would be four chatot—for not to teach extra chatot but teach Shabbat novelty even though he only fixed to remove limb from live animal as Pesachim, etc.; and outside idol worship is novelty as proven in sugya—end quote. Per this no place for above difficulty—for Pesachim what did he fix—Rashi explained not that shechitah purifies from nevelah—for nevertheless impure because of idol worship; answer to remove from limb from live animal—that is novelty Tosafot hinted; this if animal is idol-worship offering; but if animal not forbidden in idol-worship offering like mountain—no place for difficulty what did he fix—for he fixed like all slaughterings to purify from nevelah—for not impure because of offering; still Tosafot's difficulty what does counting chatot teach—and perforce deals forbidden in idol worship and teaches he fixed limb from live animal; therefore Gemara challenges well; thereby also settle difficulty why challenge R. Huna from baraita three chatot—say baraita like R. Yehoshua ben Levi who holds in baraita even in libation person does not forbid what is not his and it is great act, and R. Huna ruled like Tanna Kamma; per what I wrote one may say baraita comes to teach novelty as Tosafot—that it is corrupting since he fixed limb from live animal, therefore like R. Shimon—as R. Shimon holds corrupting in connection exempt; Rashi holds in act person forbids—as Shulchan Aruch Bava Kamma 79 regarding slaughter exempt from payments 4 and 5 because not fit shechitah—and we learn person forbids through act as Tosafot and Rashba there s.v. bishlema; therefore challenges R. Huna who holds even small act—for otherwise we would say great act; and think. Still need understand as Tosafot taught novelty of slaughter outside—as in sugya; what novelty—and if to teach R. Huna small act can forbid—this not learned from this baraita; on contrary if we say not forbidden plainly liable for slaughter outside—need not check half damaged kaneh, etc.; if so what novelty in baraita—must say we might have thought in kodshim even without any act forbidden as Rambam Hilchos Issurei Mizbeach chapter 4 halachah 6—lost kodshim forbids even friend's even without act; see Ra'avad who challenged requires act and Rambam's language implies without act—see there Kessef Mishneh Tosafot imply without act; but this baraita is refutation—for then not fit inside and no slaughter outside—and teaches much we require at least small act per Ra'avad—so much the more. But per view he does not forbid even in great act—fine difficulty what novelty chatot of slaughter outside teach; and if it itself teaches not forbidden in act—for otherwise need know from elsewhere only great act needed but great act also does not help—we did not hear perhaps helps—and idol worship and slaughter outside come as one; truly not helpful—and perforce learn elsewhere; if so no novelty; Maharsha explicitly for R. Nachman who holds even great act does not forbid—why need teach no issur in small act—for even great act does not forbid; if so difficulty what chatot of slaughter outside teach—must say reverse: always to teach extra chatot; that which ten not counted—baraita is R. Akiva who holds Chullin 102 two chatot and Shabbat only one liable; if so one may say first language for view even great act does not forbid—difficulty also should teach offering—for him difficult otherwise what chatot of slaughter outside teach as above—and perforce to teach extra chatat; that which ten not counted is R. Akiva; if so unnecessary R. Yehoshua ben Levi—for R. Yishmael b. R. Yochanan obligates two as explained in Gemara; and since not like R. Yehoshua ben Levi—fine difficulty from offering—for why R. Yehoshua ben Levi—kodshim kalim owner's money—if so should teach ten; for R. Yehoshua ben Levi obligates two although we say below reversed and R. Yehoshua ben Levi obligates one—see there Tosafot s.v. R. Akiva per conclusion need not say reversed and for R. Akiva only one liable—so much the more. Thereby settled Tiferet Shlomo's difficulty why Gemara challenges offering—why not say per view teaches although individual offering not fit on Shabbat to enter inside nevertheless liable for slaughter outside as Tosafot s.v. chayav sheloshah; strained to say should teach asham and it is never communal offering; per my view tzarich iyun—for should teach offering and instead of Shabbat teach ten—for what difference this chatot from that chatot; and further unnecessary deals communal offering ten—for he had no shelamim of congregation at all. After we clarified all this b'seder it appears Ran and Ra'ah have proof for their words—for we clarified therefore not established in act for mountain—for baraita is R. Yishmael b. R. Yochanan; therefore not teach offering; difficulty if to teach extra chatot should count ten—or teaches fixing because of oto v'et beno and learn forbidden because of sacrifices of the dead—for otherwise what did he fix; difficulty for R. Yehoshua ben Levi—is it pleasant he holds person does not forbid even in great act as Rashi—and if so still what did he answer—for no sacrifices of the dead person does not forbid and like other slaughter and much fixed—and if so still did not innovate to teach extra chatat without innovation it did not come—great fifth difficulty. Perforce Ran's rule: shechitah does not impart nevelah impurity—and what did he fix—for still impure—and perforce because of limb from live animal—and this is what Tosafot teach; therefore Ran's words required. (Tosafot Pesachim 72 challenged: idol-worship offerings impure only d'rabbanan; per this fine: certainly for impurity in tent, etc.; but here no shechitah at all—like piercing and there is nevelah impurity as before—like died by itself—think.) Also proof from Bava Kamma slaughtering for idol worship—R. Shimon exempt from payments 4 and 5 who holds unfit shechitah; Tosafot wrote even though person does not forbid through act he forbade it—should challenge from this for view even through act does not forbid as they challenged from two holding knife and impure from libation, etc.; per Ran's explanation fine: even though person does not forbid—nevertheless shechitah is only making nevelah and piercing and no payments 4 and 5. Now what Rashba challenged can be settled—first challenge say to himself: he cut in dust—for no shechitah—certainly knew deals with bird chatat from several reasons they wrote should teach offering and asham—only they thought strain distant case half kaneh damaged and he completed; per my view unnecessary—say bird chatat and slaughtered in kaneh; when became nevelah—when slaughtered majority kaneh and then slaughter completed outside—and came together; but per you any cut is sacrifices of the dead and slaughter outside not until slaughtered majority and already forbidden—tzarich iyun. Second difficulty why establish in animal chatat—impossible—for once slaughtered one siman became nevelah—one may say same as above since he holds even great act does not forbid—unnecessary teach in act he does not forbid and there is slaughter outside issur—even if he does not forbid perforce not to innovate except to teach extra chatat as above; difficulty therefore why count bird chatat impossible only in bird—should count animal chatat too and likewise other offerings; e.g. saying at completion he worshiped does not make kodshim nevelah—and if obvious even in that case obvious; on contrary here somewhat greater novelty since saying at completion does not make it nevelah beforehand; but in this form only extra chatat. (Rambam Hilchos Shegagot citing this baraita wrote e.g. saying at completion he worshiped.) Rather certainly in great act he forbids and teaches not forbidden without act; Gemara answers like his own case—and if so we might say worship forbidden relative to his case and teaches nevertheless requires act—think. If worshipper slaughtered b'shogeg thinking permitted as we find brings chatat—as mishnah libating b'shogeg—apparently “to pain” not applicable—for he thinks permitted; owner can say you are not so important I say you were intentional and intended to pain. Likewise if animal in his hand and miggo it was not slaughtered and he says it was slaughtered for idol worship and I did not intend to pain you—appears we say presumption he intended to pain and it is permitted; for otherwise why Gemara challenge from two slaughtering—mishnah only wanted to teach law of two slaughtering—and deals where slaughtered b'shogeg or has miggo and cries I did not intend to pain—and so Tosafot and Rashba challenged Bava Kamma thief slaughtering for idol worship—not established b'shogeg; or what of it we say “to pain”—not believed to say b'shogeg to cause loss to friend; think.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (ט"ז סק"ד) ותימא על הב"י. לכאורה תמי' על תמיהתו דהר"ן לא כ"כ אלא לענין אף אם אין אוסר דבר שאינו שלו מ"מ אסור באכילה דלאו איהו אסיר אלא דלא שרי אבל לפסק הש"ע דאדם אוסר דש"ש אלא דאמרינן לצעורי' מכוין בזה ל"ש סברת הר"ן דהא דאמרי' דלא שחט כלל לעבודת כוכבים וממילא גם באכילה שרי ועי' בסמוך בש"ך סק"ה:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: **(Taz seif 4) And you might wonder on Beit Yosef.** Apparently wonder on his wonder on Ran—not so, only regarding even if he does not forbid what is not his—nevertheless forbidden in eating, for he did not forbid but did not permit; but per Shulchan Aruch ruling person forbids what is not his except we say “to pain him”—Ran's reasoning does not apply—for he said he did not slaughter at all for idol worship and thereby also permitted in eating; see nearby Shach seif 5.

kaf_hachayim.he: ד) ואפ' לא שחט בה אלא סי' א' לשם ע"ז אסורה. ל"ח. כנה"ג בהגה"ט או' ב' זב"ש או' א' זב"צ או' ג'.
kaf_hachayim.en: **d) And even** if he slaughtered in it only siman 1 for idol worship—forbidden. Levush. Kenesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Taz letter 2. Zivchei Shlomo letter 1. Zivchei Tzedek letter 3.

kereti.he:
לא אסרה עיין פלתי שהארכתי כי מסקנת פוסקים אפי' במעשה זוטא יכול לאסור של חבירו. והא דיכול לאסור במעשה זוטא היינו מדרבנן ומהתורה א"י לאסור כלל וכלל. אפי' במעשה רבה.
גם בזה בח"מ סי' שפ"ה במנסך יין סותם מחבר ביש לו שותפות לא אמרינן לצערו וכאן מביא מחבר שני דיעות עי' פלתי דהעיקר כמ"ש סמ"ע דיין שאני דהא היה יכול להבדיל יין חברו לבדו ולנסכו אלו כוון לצערו משא"כ בהמה א"א לחלקם בלי שחיטה. ומסתבר הוא ועיין פלתי כי הש"ך טען עליו מדברי גמ' ואני המלצתי בעדו בטוב טעם.
לצערו אבל מ"מ שחיטתו אינו כלום דהוי כאלו לא שחט כ"כ הר"ן והט"ז הסכים וכן מהרש"ל והש"ך השיג ע"ז ועיין פלתי שישבתי כל קושי' והבאתי ראיה לדברי הר"ן ויש להחמיר בדבריו. ואם שחט בשוגג לע"ז עיין פלתי שכתבתי דמ"מ מותר דיטען איני מאמינך דה"ה בשוגג רק במזיד הי' ובאמת לצערו ועכשיו דמהדר הדר ביה ואפי' אית ליה מגו אין נאמן נגד כלל דעושה לצערו ואפשר אפי' אם הוא בא מאליו ואמת שכך שחט והי' כוונתו במתכוין לא משגיחין ביה אבל לגביה נפשיה ודאי אסור דשוי' חד"א.
הרי זה ודאי זבחי מתים ואוסר בהנאה. ואם מסר בהמת חבירו לשליח חושב שהוא שלו. ושחטו לע"ז לכ"ע אסור ולא שייך לצעורי כ"כ תוס' ב"ק דף ע"א ד"ה בשלמא וכ"כ רשב"א.
kereti.en:
He did not forbid it—see Peleti I extended that conclusion of poskim: even in small act can forbid friend's property; and that one can forbid in small act is d'rabbanan, and from Torah Israel cannot forbid at all, even in great act.
Also here Choshen Mishpat siman 385 regarding libating wine—Mechaber rules anonymously if partnership does not say “to pain him”; here Mechaber brings two views—see Peleti main point as Semag wrote wine is different—for he could separate friend's wine alone and libate it if intending to pain him, unlike animal impossible to divide without shechitah; plausible; see Peleti Shach challenged from Gemara and I defended with good reason.
To pain him—but nevertheless his shechitah is nothing—as if he did not slaughter—so Ran and Taz agreed and Maharshal; Shach challenged on this; see Peleti I settled all difficulties and brought proof for Ran's words—one should be stringent in his words. If slaughtered b'shogeg for idol worship—see Peleti I wrote nevertheless permitted—for he can claim I do not believe you—even b'shogeg only when intentional was and truly to pain him, and now he returns; even if he has miggo—not believed against general rule he acts to pain him; possible even if he comes on his own—and truly he slaughtered so and intent was intentional—we do not attend to him regarding himself certainly forbidden for he made it a doubt.
This one—certainly sacrifices of the dead and forbidden in benefit. If he gave friend's animal to agent who thinks it is his and slaughtered for idol worship—for all forbidden; “to pain him” does not apply—so Tosafot Bava Kamma 71 s.v. bishlema; and so Rashba.

mechaber.he: השוחט לשם הרים וגבעות לשם חמה ולבנה כוכבים ומזלות ימים ונהרות אין לו דין תקרובת עבודת כוכבים לאוסרה בהנאה אבל שחיטתו פסולה אע"פ שלא נתכוין לעבדם אלא לרפואה וכיוצא בה מדברי הבאי שאומרים העובדי כוכבים:
mechaber.en: One who slaughters for mountains and hills, for sun and moon, stars, days, and rivers—does not have status of idol-worship offering to forbid in benefit; but his shechitah is invalid—even if he did not intend to worship them but for healing and the like, per words of fools that idolaters say.

siftei_kohen.he:
לשם חמה ולבנה. עצמן ועי' ס"ק ט':
אין לו דין תקרובת כו'. מלשון המחבר משמע דאעפ"י שנתכוין לעבדם לא הוי אלא פסולה ולא זבחי מתים ודוק והיינו דאזיל לטעמיה שפי' כן בב"י דברי הרמב"ם אבל הרשב"א והטור פירשו דברי הרמב"ם דבמתכוין לעבדם הוי זבחי מתים וכ"פ מהרש"ל שם סימן כ"א והב"ח ואפשר לכוין גם דברי המחבר לזה וע"ל סימן קמ"א ס"א:
siftei_kohen.en:
**For sun and moon.** Themselves—and see seif 9.
**Does not have status of offering, etc.** From Mechaber's language appears that even if he intended to worship them—it is only invalid and not sacrifices of the dead—examine; and this is his view as he explained in Beit Yosef Rambam's words; but Rashba and Tur explained Rambam that when intending to worship them it is sacrifices of the dead; and so Maharshal there siman 21; and Bach; and possible to explain Mechaber's words also this way; and see below siman 141 seif 1.

turei_zahav.he:
לשם הרים. הטעם דכל אלו הם מחוברים ודרשינן אלהיהם על ההרים ולא ההרים אלהיהם:
אין לו דין כו'. זו דעת רמב"ם וס"ל במכוין לעובדו אסור אפילו בשוחט לשם הר אבל במכוין לרפואה או לשאר דברי הבאי יש חילוק בעושה כן לשם הר אינו נאסר בהנאה כיון דאפילו בשוחט לשם הר אין ההר עצמו נאסר משום עבודת כוכבים דכתיב אלהיהם על ההרים ולא ההרים אלהיהם אבל בשוחט לשם רפואה לשר של הר אסור בהנאה כיון דבשוחט ממש לשם שר נעשה עבודת כוכבים ודבר פשוט שאין איסור אלא בשוחט לשם הר אבל בשוחט בהר מותר:
turei_zahav.en:
**For mountains.** Reason: all these are attached, and we derive “their gods upon the mountains and not the mountains their gods.”
**Does not have status, etc.** This is Rambam's view, and he holds when intending to worship them forbidden even slaughtering for a mountain; but when intending for healing or other matters of fools—there is distinction: doing so for a mountain is not forbidden in benefit, since even slaughtering for a mountain the mountain itself is not forbidden for idol worship, as written “their gods upon the mountains”; but slaughtering for healing to minister of mountain—forbidden in benefit, since in slaughtering itself for minister it becomes idol worship; straightforward matter that issur is only slaughtering for mountain, but slaughtering in mountain permitted.

baer_heitev.he:
הרים. כל אלו מחוברים הם. ודרשינן אלהיהם על ההרים ולא ההרים אלהיהם:
העובדי כוכבים. וכ' בש"ך דמדברי המחבר משמע אף אם מתכוין לעבדה לא אסרה בהנאה אבל מהרש"ל והב"ח כתבו אם נתכוונו לעבדם הוי זבחי מתים ואפשר דגם דברי המחבר מסכים לזה ועיין לקמן סי' קמ"א ס"א:
baer_heitev.en:
**Mountains.** All these are attached; we derive “their gods upon the mountains.”
**Idolaters.** Shach wrote from Mechaber's words appears even if intended to worship—not forbidden in benefit; but Maharshal and Bach wrote if intended to worship them it is sacrifices of the dead; and possible Mechaber agrees; see below siman 141 seif 1.

beer_hagolah.he:
משנה שם דף ל"ט
טור וכ"כ הרשב"א ור' ירוחם והתוס' בדף מ'
ל' הרמב"ם שם ופירשו הרשב"א בת"ה והטור דבריו דאם נתכוין לעבדה הוי תקרובת עבודת כוכבים מהא דאיתא בעבודת כוכבים דף מ"ה וסנהדרין דף ס"ח דעובדי הר בסייף ואין דעת התוס' כן ע"ש
beer_hagolah.en:
Mishnah there daf 39.
Tur, and so Rashba and Rabbenu Yerucham and Tosafot daf 40.
Rambam's language there; and Rashba in Terumat HaDeshen and Tur explained his words: if intended to worship it is idol-worship offering, from that which is in Avodah Zarah 45 and Sanhedrin 68 that mountain worshippers with sword—and Tosafot's view is not so—see there.

beur_hagra.he:
(סעיף ה') לשם המה כו'. עתוס' שם ד"ה הא. והא דקתני הכא כו':
(ליקוט) אע"פ שלא כו'. עבה"ג וכ"כ בת"ה. ול"נ כנ"ל דאי במתכוין לעובדה בלא"ה אסור משום מומר (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
**(seif 5) For sun, etc.** Tosafot there s.v. ha.
**(Likkut) Even if did not intend, etc.** Bach, and so Terumat HaDeshen. And in my opinion as above: if intending to worship—nevertheless forbidden because of mumar (end).

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (שם סק"ה) וקשה א"כ אף בלא כוון. זהו קושית התוס' חולין (דף י"ד) אהא דמשנינן הב"ע בישראל מומר דא"כ בלא"ה אסור משום שחיטת מומר (והט"ז נקט לה לקושי' אף לאוקימתא דאתרו בי' ועי' בב"י במ"ש דס"ל להרמב"ם דשינוי' דמשני במומר דחוקא דא"כ בלא"ה אסור משום שחיטת מומר ודוחק לומר דמתני' בלא היה מומר מעיקרא אלא דבאותה שחיטה נעשה מומר וכגון דהתרו בו וקבל התראה וכו' משמע דס"ל להב"י דע"י ההתראה נעשה מומר אף בלא שחט לשם עבודת כוכבים אלא דמקרי מומר באותה שחיטה כיון דההתראה ע"י השחיטה. והסברא מוקשה דממ"נ אם בקיבל ההתראה לחוד בלא מעשה מקרי מומר ממילא הוי קודם השחיטה וצ"ע) והוכיחו מזה דבפעם א' לא נעשה מומר ואם כוונת המ"ז להקשות לאידך פוסקים דס"ל בפעם א' נעשה מומר איך יתרצו קושי' תוס' א"כ לא הועיל בתירוצו דנ"מ לענין הנאה הא מ"מ סוגיין לא מתרצא בהכי דהא מתני' דקתני וא' שוחט לשם א' מכל אלו שחיטתו פסולה היינו דקאי ארישא דמתני' דקתני לשם הרים דשחיטתו פסולה ואסורה באכילה ומותר בהנאה ובזה ישאר הקושיא דתיפוק ליה משום שחיטת מומר:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: **(there seif 5) And difficulty—if so even without intent.** This is Tosafot's difficulty Chullin (14) on that which we answer “owner's portion” in Israelite mumar—for otherwise forbidden because of slaughter of mumar {Taz cited this difficulty also for resolution “they warned him”; see Beit Yosef what Rambam holds change in answer in mumar is strained—if so otherwise forbidden because of slaughter of mumar; strain to say mishnah when he was not mumar from outset but became mumar in that slaughter, e.g. warned and accepted warning, etc.—appears Beit Yosef holds through warning he becomes mumar even without slaughtering for idol worship but called mumar in that slaughter since warning through slaughter; and reasoning is strained: if he accepted warning alone without act he is called mumar—automatically before slaughter—and tzarich iyun}; and they proved from this not mumar in one time; and if Maharshal's intent to challenge other poskim who hold mumar in one time—how will they answer Tosafot's difficulty—his answer did not help—for nevertheless sugya not resolved thus—for mishnah teaching one slaughtering for one of all these invalid—refers to reisha teaching for mountains invalid in eating permitted in benefit—and difficulty remains it should emerge because of slaughter of mumar.

kaf_hachayim.he: ה) ולאו דוקא סי' א' אלא אפי' שחט כל דהו מן הסי' לע"ז ג"כ אסורה עי"ז ולא מבעיא כל דהו בושט דעושה אותה נבילה אלא אפי' שחט כל דהו מן הקנה דאינו עושה אותה נבילה ג"כ אסורה כס' הש"ך בנה"כ ססי' ב' יעו"ש. אבנ במריטת הנוצות לשם ע"ז אין חשש ומ"מ אפי' במריטת הנוצות דין זה צ"ע. דע"ק או' א' וגדולי הקדש או' א' זב"צ או' ד' ועיין לקמן או' ט'.
kaf_hachayim.en: **e) And not** specifically siman 1—even slaughtering any amount of siman for idol worship forbidden thereby; and needless to say any amount in windpipe that makes nevelah; but even slaughtering any amount in kaneh that does not make nevelah—also forbidden, as Shach wrote in Nekudot HaKesef end siman 2—see there. Plucking feathers for idol worship—no concern; nevertheless even plucking feathers this law—tzarich iyun. Arukh HaShulchan letter 1. Gedolei HaKodesh letter 1. Zivchei Tzedek letter 4. And see below letter 9.

kereti.he: אע"פ וכו' דעת מחבר אפי' נתכוון לעובד' מ"מ אינו זבחי מתים ומכ"ש אם נתכוון לרפואה. וזהו באמת דעת התוס' אבל ברמב"ם משמע אם נתכוון לעובדם אף זבחי מתים הוי ואין להאריך בזה:
kereti.en: Even if, etc.—Mechaber's view: even if intended to worship—nevertheless not sacrifices of the dead, and all the more if intended for healing; this is truly Tosafot's view; but Rambam implies if intended to worship them—even sacrifices of the dead; not to expand.

mechaber.he: שחט לשם שר של הר או לשם שר א' משאר הדברים בין ששחט לשם מיכאל השר הגדול בין ששחט לשם שר של שלשול קטן שבים (פי' מין תולעת) הרי זה זבחי מתים ואסור בהנאה:
mechaber.en: For minister of a mountain, or for one minister among other things—whether he slaughtered for Michael the great minister or for minister of a small worm in the sea {species of worm}—this is sacrifices of the dead and forbidden in benefit.

siftei_kohen.he:
או לשם שר א' כו'. וחמה ולבנה יש להן ג"כ שרים כדאמרינן במדרש י"ב מלאכים מנהיגים את החמה. תוספות:
הרי זה זבחי מתים כו'. משמע דקאי אאפי' לא נתכוין לעבדם דסליק מיניה דאפ"ה הוי זבחי מתים כהרמב"ם ולא כר"י (ב' הדעות בטור ע"ש) וכ"פ מהרש"ל שם:
siftei_kohen.en:
**Or for one minister, etc.** Sun and moon also have ministers, as we say in midrash twelve angels lead the sun—Tosafot.
**This is sacrifices of the dead, etc.** Implies it refers even if he did not intend to worship them—for it ascends from him that nevertheless it is sacrifices of the dead like Rambam, not like R. Yitzchak {two views in Tur see there}; and so Maharshal there.

baer_heitev.he:
שר. וחמה ולבנה יש להם גם כן שרים דאיתא במדרש י"ב מלאכים מנהיגים את החמה:
בהנאה. וכתב בש"ך אפילו לא נתכוין לעבדם אפילו הכי הוי זבחי מתים וכן פסק מהרש"ל:
baer_heitev.en:
**Minister.** Sun and moon also have ministers—as in midrash twelve angels lead the sun.
**In benefit.** Shach wrote: even if he did not intend to worship them—even so sacrifices of the dead; and so Maharshal ruled.

beer_hagolah.he: בריית' שם דף מ' וכדמפרש שם בגמ'
beer_hagolah.en: Baraita there daf 40, as explained there in Gemara.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (שם סק"ה) ותימא שהוא נגד הש"ס דחולין. לענ"ד לא קשה מידי דהא מתחלה פרכי' על ר"נ ור"ע ורי"צ דאמרי אין אדם אוסר דש"ש מההיא דמנסך ותירצו דמיירי בשותפות. ואח"כ אמרי' דר"נ ור"ע אמרי אפי' למ"ד אדם אוסר דש"ש הנ"מ עובד כוכבים אבל ישראל לצעורי מכוין. וממילא אף למ"ד אא"א דש"ש קיימא הסברא דלצעורי היכי דיש נפקותא בזה דהא לענין סברת דלצעורי לא פליגי. ולזה פרכי' ממנסך והיינו לר"נ דס"ל דאין א"א דש"ש. וגם ס"ל סברת לצעורי ממילא אף דאית ליה שותפות בגווי'. זהו מספיק לענין איסור דשאינו שלו אבל מ"מ נימא לצעורי. ובזה ל"ש סברת הסמ"ע דאלו עבד לצעורי היה לו לחלוק תחלה היין ולהציל את שלו דהא כיון דאין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו אלו יחלקו השותפות לא יאסר ולא הי' בידו לצעורי לחבירו לאסור יינו ע"י קיום השותפות אבל לדינא דקיי"ל דאין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו קיימא סברת הסמ"ע לנכון ודו"ק:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: **(there seif 5) And you might wonder he is against Shas Chullin.** Per my view no difficulty—for initially they challenged R. Nachman and R. Akiva and R. Yitzchak who say person does not forbid what is not his from libation; and they answered it deals with partnership. And afterward they said R. Nachman and R. Akiva say even per view person forbids what is not his—difference gentile, but Israel “to pain him.” And thereby even per view person does not forbid what is not his—the reasoning “to pain him” applies where there is relevance—for regarding reasoning of “to pain him” they do not dispute. Therefore they challenged from libation—and this is for R. Nachman who holds person does not forbid what is not his; and he also holds reasoning of “to pain him”; therefore even though he has partnership inside—sufficient for issur of what is not his; but nevertheless we say “to pain him.” And in this no place Semag's reasoning that if he acted to pain he should have separated wine first and saved his own—for since person does not forbid what is not his, if they divide partnership he will not forbid and he had no ability to pain friend by forbidding wine through maintaining partnership; but for law we hold person does not forbid what is not his—Semag's reasoning stands correctly; think.

kaf_hachayim.he: ו) ודע דבעכו"ם לא כתיב אלא ג' עבודות דהיינו שחיטה וזריקה והקטרה ולפיכך אינה נפסלת בשחיטה אלא א"כ חישב בשעת שחיטה לזרוק דמה או להקטיר חלבה לעכו"ם אבל אם חישב לעבודות אחרות לא פסלה. פר"ח או' א' וכ"כ השמ"ח או' ב' דאינה נפסלת אלא בג' עבודות הנז' אבל אם חשב בשחיטה לקבל הדם או להוליך הדם לשם ע"ז ולא להקריבו לפניה לא נאסרה הבהמה. וס"ד בדידעינן בההוא גברא דידע שאין זה עבודה שחייבים עליה בע"ז אבל בלא"ה חיישינן שמא הוכיח מחשבה זו שגם שחיטתו היה לע"ז עכ"ד.
kaf_hachayim.en: **f) And know** with gentile only three avodot are written—shechitah, throwing, and burning; therefore not disqualified in shechitah unless he thought at shechitah to throw blood or burn fat for idol worship; but if he thought for other avodot—did not disqualify. Peri Chadash letter 1. And so Shulchan Malachim letter 2—not disqualified except in three avodot mentioned; but if he thought at shechitah to receive blood or carry blood toward idol worship and not sacrifice before it—animal not forbidden. And mistake in our understanding in that man who knew this is not avodah liable for idol worship—but in any case we are concerned perhaps this thought proved also his shechitah was for idol worship—end quote.

kereti.he:
לשם שר וכוכבי לכת וי"ב מזלות כולם יש להם ממונים המנהגים אותם וזהו הי' כשופים בזמניהם שהי' מקטירים לשרים משל כוכבי' שמים ובזמנינו רבו המתפרצים וצוחקים על זה ואומרים כי הכוכבי שמים הם מקשים ואין בם רוח ואין להם מנהיג רק הושם בם טבע סיבוב לתנועה ובעו"ה איש בדרך ישר בעינו ילך וגורם כפירות הרבה בתורה
זבחי מתים אפי' לרפוא' והיינו מדרבנן:
kereti.en:
For minister and planets and twelve constellations—all have appointees leading them—this was like sorcerers in their time who burned incense to ministers corresponding to heavenly bodies; in our time transgressors multiplied and mock, saying heavenly bodies are hard matter without spirit and no leader—only nature of rotation was placed in them; woe—man goes in his straight way and causes much denial of Torah.
Sacrifices of the dead—even for healing—and this is d'rabbanan.

mechaber.he: ישמעאלים שאינם מניחים ישראל לשחוט אלא אם כן יהפוך פניו לא"ל קיבל"א (דהיינו שיהפוך פניו נגד מזרח) כמנהג חקותיהם אינו דומה לשוחט לשם הרים. ומכל מקום ראוי לבטל המנהג ההוא ולגעור במי שעושה כן (הואיל ומקפידים על כך) (רשב"א סימן שמ"ה):
mechaber.en: Ishmaelites who do not let an Israelite slaughter unless he turns his face to kebla {meaning: turn his face toward the east} per their custom—is not like one who slaughters for mountains. Nevertheless it is proper to abolish that custom and rebuke one who does so {since they are stringent about this (Rashba siman 245)).}

siftei_kohen.he: אינו דומה לשוחט לשם הרים. דהתם השוחט עצמו מתכוין לכך אבל הכא זה מחשב וזה עובד לא אמרינן. רשב"א:
siftei_kohen.en: **Not like slaughtering for mountains.** For there the slaughterer himself intends so; but here “this one thinks and this one acts” we do not say—Rashba.

turei_zahav.he: אינו דומה לשוחט לשם הרים. הטעם דאפילו בשוחט לשם הרים אין איסור אלא כששוחט עצמו נתכוין לשם הרים אבל זה שוחט וזה עובד לא אמרינן כדלעיל סעיף ג' וג"כ אין כאן איסור מצד הרואה דהרואה סבור דאתרמי ליה אותו צד ואינו עושה כן בכוונה:
turei_zahav.en: **Not like slaughtering for mountains.** Reason: even slaughtering for mountains issur only when slaughterer himself intended for mountains; but here “this one thinks and this one acts” we do not say, as above seif 3; and also no issur from viewer's side—for viewer thinks that side happened by chance and he does not do so intentionally.

baer_heitev.he: כך. וכתב בט"ז דאינו דומה לשוחט לשם הרים דזה מחשב וזה עובד לא אמרינן וגם אין לאסור מפני מראית עין מפני שהרואה סבר דאיתרמי ליה אותו צד ואינו עושה כן בכוונה:
baer_heitev.en: **So.** Taz wrote: not like slaughtering for mountains—“this one thinks and this one acts” we do not say; and also not to forbid because of marit ayin—for viewer thinks that side happened by chance and he does not do so intentionally.

beur_hagra.he:
(סעיף ז') אינו דומה כו'. כמש"ש ל"ה ב' זה מחשב וזה עובד כו':
ומ"מ כו'. דדומה קצת לשוחט לתוך ימים ולתוך גומא דאיכא משום מראית העין:
הואיל כו'. אבל בלא"ה אמרינן מקום הוא דלא אתרמי ליה כמש"ש י"ג א'.
beur_hagra.en:
**(seif 7) Not similar, etc.** As written 35b: “this one thinks and this one acts,” etc.
**Nevertheless, etc.** For it is somewhat like slaughtering into seas and into pit—for there is marit ayin.
**Since, etc.** But in any case we say it is a place that did not happen to him, as written 13a.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (בא"ד) דס"ל להטור והמחבר כהר"ן. והא דבאינו שותף אינו אוסר. היינו לא דס"ל להלכתא כר"ן. אלא בדרך סניף כיון דלרמב"ם ורש"י דלאו הכי בשותפות ל"א לצעורי. משום הכי ס"ל להכרעה בצירוף סברת הר"ן דאסור באכילה משום הכי פסק כן בשותפות בדרך צירוף הסברות:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: **(in gloss) That Tur and Mechaber hold like Ran.** And that when not partner he does not forbid—meaning not that halachah is like Ran; rather as branch: since for Rambam and Rashi not so regarding partnership—“to pain him” does not apply; therefore he holds ruling combining Ran's reasoning forbidden in eating—therefore ruled so regarding partnership by combining reasonings.

kaf_hachayim.he: ז) שם. לזרוק דמה וכו' וה"ה להקטיר מבשרה לע"ז. ט"ז סק"א. שמ"ח או' ב' פר"ת או' א' מש"ז או' א' והיינו להקטיר כזית מבשרה לע"ז. פר"ת שם. זב"צ או' ה'.
kaf_hachayim.en: **g) There. To throw blood, etc.** Likewise burning from its meat for idol worship—Taz seif 1. Shulchan Malachim letter 2. Peri Toar letter 1. Shulchan Malachim letter 1. And this is burning olive-size from its meat for idol worship—Peri Toar there. Zivchei Tzedek letter 8.

kereti.he: אינו דומה מכמה טעמים וגם זה מחשב וזה עובד לא אמרינן:
kereti.en: Not similar for several reasons; and also “this one thinks and this one acts” we do not say.
